detail: Resolves the contested case. The Auditor General of Trinidad and Tobago, the Bank's statutory auditor under the Central Bank Act, declined appointment: the Central Bank reported that the Office 'would not be in a position to accept an appointment as auditor' for the year ended 30 September 2024. The Bank states that 'BDO T&T replaced the Auditor General as the external auditor of the Bank for the financial year beginning October 1, 2023', with that initial engagement ending 30 September 2024. So: statutory auditor is the Auditor General (state audit body), work actually done by BDO T&T (private firm). A separate Guardian report of the same period records Prime Minister Kamla Persad-Bisessar instructing the Finance Minister to have the accounts audited by the Auditor General under section 51 of the Central Bank Act; that article does not report the instruction being carried out, so BDO T&T remains the last named auditor on the record.
source_title: Auditor General declined to audit Central Bank (Trinidad and Tobago Guardian)

detail: Named by statute, not by a published auditor's report. Central Bank of Myanmar Law (Pyidaungsu Hluttaw Law No. 16/2013), section 36(b): 'The accounts of the Central Bank shall be audited by the Union Auditor General Office at least once a year.' Section 36(c) further requires the year-end balance sheet and profit and loss statement to be certified by the Union Auditor General. Section 36(a) covers quarterly internal audit by the Bank's own Internal Audit Department. No published CBM financial statements carrying a signed auditor's report were found; the record rests on the statute naming a specific body.
source_title: Central Bank of Myanmar Law 2013 (Pyidaungsu Hluttaw Law No. 16/2013), unofficial English translation
